# `highpass`

a zero-phase high-pass filter, written as a new recording.

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run highpass --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run highpass --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run highpass --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --lower 1
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `recording` | field recording, each true, where {"name": "$recording"} | yes |
| `mean` | measurement mean, of recording, where {"name": "$mean_over"}, required false (the record's channel means: `nxr-neuro run measure --set channel_span_mean --all` first) | no |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recording` | `--recording` | `none` | - |  | the recording's name, or none: every recording of the subject, one run each |
| `mean_over` | `--mean-over` | none | - |  | the selection the channel means were measured over, by name; null: the one that holds them |
| `name` | `--name` | `{recording}_highpass` | - |  | the new recording's name |
| `lower` | `--lower` | none | Hz |  | the high-pass edge |
| `method` | `--method` | none | - |  | fir \| iir; null: the reference's (FIR, but IIR for bandstop and notch) |
| `ripple` | `--ripple` | none | - |  | FIR: the passband and stopband deviation (linear); null: 1e-3 |
| `transition` | `--transition` | none | Hz |  | FIR: each transition band; null: the reference's rule |
| `edge` | `--edge` | none | - |  | FIR: the record's ends padded with the mean of the transient (mean_of_transient) or zeros; null: mean_of_transient |
| `transient_samples` | `--transient-samples` | none | samples |  | FIR: the transient's length stated; null: the energy rule |
| `remove_mean` | `--remove-mean` | none | - |  | FIR: subtract the record's channel means first; null: true |
| `notch_bandwidth` | `--notch-bandwidth` | none | Hz |  | IIR notch: each notch's 3-dB bandwidth; null: 1 Hz |
| `bandstop_order` | `--bandstop-order` | none | - |  | IIR bandstop: the Butterworth prototype's order; null: 4 |
| `tolerance` | `--tolerance` | none | - |  | IIR: the decayed tail the look-behind and look-ahead may leave out; null: 1e-15 |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| chunks over `recording` | [`signal.filter`](../nodes.md) | x=recording, mean=mean | kind=highpass, lower=$lower, method=$method, ripple=$ripple, transition=$transition, edge=$edge, transient_samples=$transient_samples, remove_mean=$remove_mean, notch_bandwidth=$notch_bandwidth, bandstop_order=$bandstop_order, tolerance=$tolerance | y |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `y` | kind recording, name $name, description a zero-phase high-pass filter |

## Notes from the definition

```text
A ZERO-PHASE HIGH-PASS FILTER OF A RECORDING, WRITTEN AS A NEW RECORDING: each block filtered with the halo the design needs (look-behind, look-ahead), the record's ends padded as
the option set says (Brainstorm's process_bandpass / process_notch: kaiserord + fir1, or a filtfilt IIR). The whole recording is filtered (--all): a filter makes a recording.
A FIR filter that removes the record's mean reads the channel means (`nxr-neuro run measure --set channel_span_mean --all` first), or remove_mean false. The new recording carries over the
source's channel flags, events, bad segments and projectors.

  nxr-neuro run highpass --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --recording rest --all --lower 1
```
